technical_and_design_decisions: Base development on Java 17 to align with Spring Framework 6.0 runtime requirements
Follow existing Spring XD plugin patterns (Spark, RxJava) for the Reactor processor plugin to ensure consistency with the codebase
Use Protobuf 3.x for the codec implementation as it is the latest stable version compatible with Java 17 and natively supports nested object serialization
Leverage existing Zookeeper client libraries already used in Spring XD YARN deployments for admin port query functionality to avoid adding new dependencies
Target Ambari 2.7+ for the plugin implementation as it is the widely used version for Hadoop ecosystem clusters and supports custom service definitions
Implement message header tracking as a configurable enricher module to allow users to enable/disable specific header fields as needed
Use JMH (Java Microbenchmark Harness) for performance testing of complex object processing to ensure accurate and reliable benchmark results
Add validation logic at both the metadata level (JdbcHdfsOptionsMetadata) and runtime for partitioned JDBC jobs to enforce option constraints and provide clear error messages to users
assumptions: Existing Spring XD YARN deployment scripts, Zookeeper integration, and core processor plugin infrastructure are already implemented and available for modification, no need to build these from scratch
Project Reactor 3.x is compatible with Spring XD's existing module API, with no required changes to the core framework to support Reactor processors
All test environments (YARN cluster, Zookeeper instance, Ambari server) are pre-configured and available for integration and performance testing
Protobuf 3.x generated classes for test fixtures are available or can be generated from provided .proto files during test setup
The existing JDBC job module code is stable and only requires additional validation logic and documentation, no core functionality changes are needed
Users have access to the Spring XD wiki platform to view the updated partitioned job documentation
No cross-cutting changes to core Spring XD framework code are required for any of the specified user stories, all changes are limited to plugins, modules, scripts, and documentation
